title: File Management
description: A comprehensive knowledge package on organizing files and folders using a hierarchical file system with proper naming conventions. Covers file systems, naming standards, folder organization, file operations, and storage management for Grade 9 students.
subject: Digital Literacy
learningObjective: Organize files and folders using a hierarchical file system with proper naming conventions.

concepts.name: File System
concepts.description: The hierarchical structure of folders and files on a computer, organizing data in a tree-like directory layout from root to subfolders

concepts.name: File Naming Conventions
concepts.description: Rules and best practices for naming files clearly and consistently to ensure findability, avoid conflicts, and maintain professionalism

concepts.name: Folder Organization
concepts.description: Creating logical folder structures with meaningful hierarchy to organize work, projects, and resources for efficient retrieval

concepts.name: File Operations
concepts.description: Fundamental actions performed on files including copying, moving, renaming, deleting, and creating shortcuts or aliases

concepts.name: Storage Management
concepts.description: Understanding different storage types—hard drives, SSDs, cloud storage—and implementing backup strategies to prevent data loss

definitions.definition: A collection of data stored on a computer with a name and type, such as a document, image, or program
A container that holds files and other folders in a hierarchical structure, also called a directory
The address of a file showing its location from root to the file, such as C:\Documents\Homework\essay.docx
The suffix after a filename that indicates the file type, such as .txt, .jpg, .pdf, or .docx
A copy of files stored separately from the original to prevent data loss in case of hardware failure, accidental deletion, or disaster

examples.title: Documents Folder
examples.description: An organized Documents folder structured by project name, then by date, with clear file names like 2026-08-05_science-report.docx instead of untitled1.docx

examples.title: Google Drive
examples.description: A cloud file storage service that allows folder sharing, real-time collaboration, and access from any device with an internet connection

examples.title: Windows File Explorer
examples.description: The built-in file management tool in Windows with a preview pane, search functionality, and quick access to frequently used folders

examples.title: macOS Finder
examples.description: Apple's file manager featuring color-coded tags for categorization, smart folders that auto-organize files by rules, and a column view for navigating hierarchies

examples.title: External Hard Drive
examples.description: A portable physical storage device used for backing up important files, transferring data between computers, and archiving old projects

misconceptions.belief: Saving and exporting are the same
misconceptions.correction: Saving overwrites the current file with changes. Exporting creates a new file in a different format, such as saving a Word document as a PDF.

misconceptions.belief: I don't need to organize, I can just search
misconceptions.correction: Good organization saves time and prevents lost files. Search works best when files are already structured logically, and it cannot help if files are misnamed or misplaced.
Cloud storage is convenient for access and sharing but is not a complete backup strategy. Files can be accidentally deleted from the cloud, accounts can be compromised, and services can shut down.

exercises.prompt: What is a file extension and why is it important when managing files on a computer?
exercises.solution: A file extension is the suffix after a filename that indicates the file type (e.g., .txt, .jpg). It is important because it tells the operating system which program to use to open the file and helps users identify file types at a glance.

exercises.prompt: Explain why consistent file naming is important for a student managing homework across multiple subjects. Give three examples of good file names.
Describe your current file organization system. What works well? What could be improved? How would you reorganize your files if you started fresh today?

Design and implement a complete folder structure for a school project that includes a research paper, presentation slides, images, and reference materials. Create the actual folders on your computer and document the structure with a screenshot or diagram.
True or False: A backup is a copy of files stored separately from the original to prevent data loss. Explain your answer.
exercises.solution: True. A backup is specifically designed to be a separate copy so that if the original files are lost due to hardware failure, accidental deletion, or disaster, the backup copy can be restored.
